quote: Yeah. So there's gonna be, like, an energy hike with the grid. So we're just kinda trying to be proactive with that and stuff.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a strong forward-looking anchor (anticipated rate hike) but the rep only affirms it generically rather than tying it back later to urgency for the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the customer already self-motivated and chose not to over-sell given a hard-DQ-free, cooperative lead.
coaching_implication: Reflect the rate-hike concern back at booking ('get ahead of that increase before it hits') to convert the stated reason into forward pull.

quote: 200. Okay. And then it's supposed to climb quite a bit with the the spike there.
stewart_read: Rep captured the $200 bill and made a light attempt to connect it to the customer's own rate-hike concern, but never flipped it into an emotional villain-frame against the utility later in the call.
coaching_implication: This was the moment to flip: 'so that $200 becomes your floor, not your ceiling, once AEP raises rates' — rep stopped short.

quote: Yes. My wife. Your wife? Okay. Awesome. Yeah. I just wanna make sure she's involved, obviously, when we give the estimate.
stewart_read: Rep correctly flagged the wife as a co-owner and stated intent to include her early, following protocol rather than treating it as an objection.
coaching_implication: Good early flag; the follow-through at booking (06:22-07:03) didn't fully close the loop.

quote: next week would probably be better if we could do that.
stewart_read: Customer softly deflected the next-day ask; rep did not concede to vague timing and instead pinned a specific day, which is the correct move.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read would say rep 'gave up' on tomorrow, but rep immediately pursued a locked day instead, supporting strategic persistence.
coaching_implication: Model this narrowing sequence (vague ask → specific day → specific time) for other reps handling 'next week' deflections.

quote: Maybe seven. I'm not sure on her schedule because she has, like, she's the best student.
stewart_read: Wife's attendance was never firmly confirmed — customer hedges twice ('probably not', 'not sure on her schedule') and the rep proceeds to lock 7PM without getting a firmer commitment or a backup plan if she can't make it.
coaching_implication: Should have asked customer to confirm with wife directly before ending the call, or set a conditional callback if she can't attend.

quote: Yeah. I mean, if something comes up, something comes up, we'll plan on 7PM on Tuesday,
stewart_read: Rep locked a day/time but never ran the 'is that fair' handshake or the no-driving/computer instruction — button_up completed only 3 of 4 parts per verified events.
coaching_implication: Add the explicit computer/no-driving line and a verbal handshake before ending — this is what keeps a booked slot from becoming a no-show.
